question.text: Meera Kulkarni holds 100 shares of Reliance at Rs. 2,500 each. She buys a 1-month Rs. 2,500-strike put at a premium of Rs. 40 per share. If at expiry Reliance is at Rs. 2,300, what is the net P&L on the position (ignore fees/tax)?

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Stock loss: 100 × (2500-2300) = Rs. 20,000. Put gain: 100 × (2500-2300) = Rs. 20,000. Premium paid: 100 × 40 = Rs. 4,000. Net = –20,000 + 20,000 – 4,000 = Rs. 4,000 loss (= premium cost). **The Trap:** Protective put caps downside at the premium paid — not at zero. 20,000 loss misses the put payoff entirely. **Cross-Exam Context:** VIII covers option payoffs; XXI-B layers on the portfolio-insurance framing. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Maximum loss on a fully-hedged protective put = put premium. You pay this insurance cost regardless of outcome.
